I will keep my plan simple and low-risk. In Quzhou County, the most dependable path for me is still the North China Plain pattern: winter wheat followed by summer maize on most of my land, and a smaller area of spring peanut to spread risk and keep some cash income. I am 50, I do not want to gamble on specialty crops that need more market information, stricter management, or harder labor organization. Wheat and maize match my experience, the local machinery, and the water conditions I know how to handle. Peanut gives me some rotation benefit and another income source, but I will not let it take over too much area because grain is still my base.

I will put most of my effort into getting stable yield rather than chasing the highest yield. For wheat, I will use improved seed, base fertilizer plus topdressing nitrogen, irrigate at the key stages, and control weeds and disease in a routine way. After wheat harvest, I will quickly plant summer maize with hybrid seed because that is where I trust yield performance the most. I will keep fertilizer moderate, not excessive, because too much input raises cost and does not always pay back. On the peanut land, I will use rotary tillage, pay more attention to plant stand and drainage, and keep pesticide sprays limited unless pressure is obvious. My whole plan is to protect income, keep field work manageable, and avoid making mistakes from doing too many different things at once.
